A mortgage is a type of loan used to purchase a property, such as a house or apartment. It is a long-term loan that is typically paid back over a period of 15 to 30 years.

When you apply for a mortgage, the lender will evaluate your creditworthiness, income, and other factors to determine how much they are willing to loan you. They will also determine your interest rate, which is the percentage of the loan that you will be paying in interest every year.

Once approved, you will receive a lump sum of money that you can use to purchase your property. You will then begin making regular payments to the lender, typically on a monthly basis. These payments will consist of a portion of the principal (the amount you borrowed) and interest.

Over time, you will gradually pay off the principal and the interest, which means that you will build equity in your property. Equity is the difference between the value of your property and the amount you owe on your mortgage.

If you fail to make your mortgage payments, the lender may foreclose on your property, which means that they will take possession of it and sell it to recover their losses. Therefore, it is important to ensure that you can afford your mortgage payments before applying for a mortgage.
